title: What counts as Python, and how the gate decides
summary: Python means .py, .pyw and .pyi files; files whose #! line names python (a rename does not hide one); and .rex, .rexx, .cls, .orx and .sh files with a line that runs python on a script, -m, -c or -u. Words, comments and 'echo python' are not calls. Anything under vendor/, upstream/ or third_party/ is exempt (third-party code carried unchanged) but is listed in the report. .git/ is never scanned. Exit codes: 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 usage error; with --advisory it always exits 0. The JSON report (alchemy.python-gate.report/1) goes to stdout and the progress log to stderr. In Autobuild v0.5.3, config key python_gate is 'enforce' by default or 'advisory'. If the gate cannot run (no rexx, script missing), the test fails: an unavailable check is NOT RUN, never PASS.
invariants: The check is lexical: a string that spells out a Python command line counts as a call (the gate's own tests carry such fixtures, and justify them).
A gate that cannot run fails closed.
